intro: Ezekiel was a priest taken to Babylon in exile, where he saw astonishing visions of God's glory.
Chapters one to twenty-four warn that Jerusalem will fall, and show God's glory leaving the temple. Chapters twenty-five to thirty-two speak to the nations.
Chapters thirty-three to forty-eight bring hope: a new heart, dry bones brought to life, and a new temple with a river flowing from it.
Tradition holds that Ezekiel wrote it himself.
Its visions are strange and vivid, so listen for the big picture: God's glory leaves, and God's glory returns.
